schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE SYSTEM DEVICE — the rack-mount device that owns the host's SYSTEM predicates and serves them device-independently. It owns host-resource data (CPU, memory, disk) and ADVERTISES the probes it can serve against them ('I accept a cpu_threshold probe, takes a value'). A caller SUBSCRIBES ('I'll take one, value 80, here's my probe address'); the system device RESOLVES ITS OWN METHOD internally (the caller never learns object.object.method), evaluates the predicate LOCALLY (Law 6 — the trigger reads the host metric INSIDE the device; the caller never sees the raw number), and its SHIM pokes the subscriber on the heartbeat pulse when the line is crossed. `SystemRackmountDevice` subclasses `BaseDevice` (CP1-CP6, Form v0 #2, on which the probe menu is advertised); `SystemRackmountShim` subclasses `BaseShim` and fires the subscriptions on the beat. It is NOT a central scheduler — scheduling is the universal heartbeat + shim + probe mechanism. SCOPE, widened by Akien 2026-08-04 and much larger than the host-resource framing above: 'any system service that isn't just a python library primitive, and even many of those... will be available thru the system rackmount.' So CPU/memory/disk are ONE tenant of this door, not its subject. The resource framing is what this charter led with, and it is what made a reader (CC, 2026-08-04) take the menu for a resource menu and move to build memory/disk — while both consumers actually named want neither.
why: So no device is coupled to the host, and no host metric is exported just to be tested (Law 6): any device can get a trigger on a host resource, but the reading STAYS HOME — only the wake-up (the poke) crosses the bus. The OS-specific backing of a host reading (load average vs a richer sampler; and, in the same family, privilege via sudo_relay) is swapped BEHIND the advertised probes without changing any device that depends on them. This is 'abstract host services device-independently' made concrete — and it corrects the goof: the system rackmount is NOT the rack (the rack is the chassis: bus + shims), and it is NOT a central scheduler (the interval/date/quantity/state enum + the SchedulerService were deleted). It is simply the OWNER of one kind of data other devices want triggers on.
invoke: Construct: `dev = SystemRackmountDevice(sampler=None)` (inject a sampler in proofs). Inspect offerings: `dev.advertises()`. Subscribe: `dev.subscribe('cpu_threshold', address='ops/personal', why=..., value=80)` → a subscription id. Wire it to the beat: `shim = SystemRackmountShim(dev, bus); ground_loop.subscribe(shim)` — the shim pokes subscribers whose line is crossed on each `beat`. Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/system_rackmount/proofs/test_system_rackmount.py` (exit 0 = green). Prove the diagnostic producer (bare, no bus): `python3 cairn/devices/system_rackmount/proofs/test_diagnostic_emit.py`.
entry: FRESH design to Form v0. The METAPHOR is quarried from UU (a rack holds rack-mount devices; a bus connects them; system services are abstracted so devices are portable), but the shape is Cairn's: a BaseDevice that OWNS host-resource data and ADVERTISES probes on it, resolving its own method so a caller stays ignorant of internals, and poking through the shared heartbeat + bus rather than a bespoke scheduler. What is NEW and Cairn's: advertise → subscribe → poke as the registration protocol; Law-6-local-evaluation (the host metric never leaves the device); the system device as a data-OWNER, not a service-registry or scheduler.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7)
filed_edges: (a) only cpu_threshold is advertised (dependency-free load-average sampler); memory/disk predicates are the SAME shape and mount when a consumer asks
(b) subscriptions are LEVEL-triggered (poke while the predicate holds); edge-triggering and unsubscribe wait on a real need
(c) advertise/subscribe are direct calls today; expressing them as bus messages (like the poke already is) is a filed edge
(d) the real host sampler (rich per-core CPU, memory, disk) is the OS-specific backing this device will own — a thin edge; the predicate physics is proven by injection
(e) sudo_relay (privilege) is a host service in this same family, built standalone first — it migrates behind this abstraction when a second consumer makes the seam pay

(f) the line-crossing/POKE emit (the flake-adjacent event) is NOT yet instrumented: the poke fires in BaseShim._fire (the shim is the diagnostic RECEIVER, not an emitter) and level eval is per-pulse (a firehose); a device-side fire-hook or edge-detection grows when a real flake needs watching. subscribe (rare, low-frequency) is the one clean device-side gate today

known_consumers.why_this_field_exists: Edge (a) says the menu grows 'when a consumer asks' — and had nowhere to record that a consumer was ALREADY NAMED. Akien named one in conversation; it was not written down BECAUSE THERE WAS NO FIELD FOR IT, and the charter went on reading as though nobody had asked. Re-stated by him 2026-08-04: 'i already know who one of the consumers is, and have told you, but since that wasn't a field, you didn't write it down.' Zero subscriptions exist in the codebase today (measured 2026-08-04: every reference to this component outside it is its own proofs, MAP.md prose, or a docstring naming it as an example). That is EXPECTED — this is a known design requirement whose consumers arrive later — not a defect and not evidence that nothing is needed.

consumers.who: CC's shim, specifically — and Akien's generalization the same breath: 'most shims will, for that same reason.' So this is a BaseShim-wide need, not one tenant's.
consumers.needs: TIME INTERRUPTS — a periodic wake so a shim can handle its mail. Cairn has NO DAEMONS; a shim that must process mail on a beat rather than on an external call needs something to interrupt it on time.
consumers.stated_by: Akien, in conversation. Re-stated 2026-08-04; the ORIGINAL statement predates this record and its date was not captured — which is the loss this field exists to stop.
consumers.what_it_costs_the_menu: This consumer wants NEITHER cpu, memory, NOR disk. Edge (a) frames the menu's growth in the resource direction and every candidate it names is resource-shaped; the known need is a TIME predicate. Building memory/disk first would have served nobody who has actually asked.

consumers.needs: THREE things now, and only the first fits what is built. (1) Timekeeping — the same beat need as the shims above, which makes TIME the first menu item with more than one named consumer. (2) ADMISSION CONTROL, Akien 2026-08-04: 'he will do things like check the system rackmount for current cpu or memory usage before launching another parallel task. same with building tasks.' This is the FIRST NAMED CONSUMER FOR MEMORY — edge (a) said memory/disk mount 'when a consumer asks', and one just asked. (3) HIS RESEARCH TASKS — reaching OUTSIDE the box, including being notified when a planned research paper hits some server. That is an EXTERNAL WATCH, not a host reading: the event's source is off-box entirely.
consumers.stated_by: Akien, 2026-08-04, across two statements: 'the librarian is another... not only for timekeeping but for his research tasks' and 'the librarian, unlike you, does not have to be a turn based device. i plan to aim closer to a human temporary working memory... he will need to keep track of research plans, and callbacks to how different research tasks are going, maybe even wanting to be notified when a planned research paper hits some server. we can't imagine yet all the things he will be tasked to do.' The last clause is load-bearing: this consumer's menu needs are OPEN by declaration, so a menu closed to what is listed today is closed against a stated design fact.
consumers.what_it_costs_the_menu: The advertised shape today is THRESHOLD-on-a-metric evaluated ON THE PULSE ('takes: [value]', `_over(metric, value)`, fired by the shim) — subscribe now, get poked LATER. Admission control needs an answer NOW, at the instant before launching. Same predicate, different moment. A research task fits neither: it is a request to DO something outside, not a predicate that goes true. So the menu is being asked to hold at least three shapes — poke-me-later, answer-me-now, and watch-something-off-box — and holds exactly one.

known_consumers.the_line_on_python_primitives: Akien's scope clause says 'even many of' the library primitives come through this door, which needs a discriminator or it is unbounded. PRIOR ART, IN HOUSE, ALREADY WRITTEN — CairnCommons/questions/what-governs-this-and-who-owns-it.json, 2026-07-22: 'THE ANSWER TO HOW FAR DOWN IS NOT DEPTH — IT IS GOVERNANCE. A tool becomes a SEAM when it HOLDS, GATES, or EXPIRES something of ours. Postgres holds a verdict record: seam. The harness expires our transcripts: seam. json.dumps produces a value and owns nothing: not a seam, no intention needed — ever, not merely not now.' That rule sorts exactly the set the scope clause gestures at, it is checkable per TOOL rather than per call, and it is a year older than this question. Recorded as the CANDIDATE discriminator and EXPLICITLY UNRULED — Akien has not been shown this connection and has not agreed the same line governs both.
known_consumers.open_and_not_decided_here: WHERE a time interrupt is served from — this device, or the ground loop (whose charter says heartbeat only, with the shim firing callbacks and waking its device). Recorded as the consumer's stated need, not adjudicated: naming the caller is this field's job, placing the predicate is not.
known_consumers.the_access_mode_the_consumers_need: ASK, not READ — and the distinction is forced by physics already declared here. Admission control reads naturally as 'give me current cpu/memory', but that EXPORTS THE READING, which this device's own advertised copy forbids in as many words: 'your value never leaves as a number (Law 6)'. The shape that keeps both halves is the caller asking ITS OWN question — 'is there room for one more, by MY line?' — which the device resolves locally and answers yes/no. The caller owns the line and owns what it does with the answer; the device owns the reading. NO NEW MACHINERY: `_resolve` already returns the predicate and `subscribe` hands it to a probe fired on each pulse; an `ask` is that same predicate evaluated once, immediately. One call, same menu, same `advertises()`. FILED, not built — the ask surface does not exist today (measured 2026-08-04: the only paths in are `advertises()` and `subscribe()`; `_reading()` is private and nothing pulls it). BUILT 2026-08-04: `ask(name, value) -> bool` on this device. It resolves through the SAME `_resolve` the subscribe door uses, so a pull and a push on one menu item cannot drift apart; the proof drives one device across one changing reading and requires the two doors to agree on every value, in both directions. The verdict-not-number claim is proven as a TYPE (`type(v) is bool`), not by scanning the returned value for the reading's digits — that scan passes for every possible bool, and a check that cannot fail proves nothing.
known_consumers.no_manager_no_count: RULED by Akien, 2026-08-04, cutting off a line of inquiry mid-search. Asked who owns a count of live builders: 'nothing does and nothing will. that would be a manager. each device will simply own it's own task of checking to see if it can start building given the available resources.' Then the sharpening, same breath: 'the harbor master is the only thing that can keep an eye on everything, including making lists from active data for display purposes. but it doesn't manage, it just reports.' THE LINE IS NOT THE COLLECTION, IT IS THE DEPENDENCY. A list of every live builder is PERMITTED — harbor_master alone may hold it, and may compile it from active data, because it is SHOWN and nothing acts on it. It becomes a manager the moment any device's decision routes through it: the instant a builder asks 'may I launch?' and something other than itself answers. This is harbor_master's own charter phrase — 'decision local, record central, execution never here' — extended from settled boats to live readings. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS DEVICE, unchanged: admission control never consults a census. The folkloric number ('more than around 6 of you and the system starts to crawl. more than 8 and we start heading for a hard crash' — Akien, MEASURED FROM EXPERIENCE, written down here for the first time; grep found it nowhere in either repo before 2026-08-04) DOES NOT NEED TO BE COUNTED. The count was a hand-proxy for pressure: six builders crawl the box BECAUSE six builders exhaust it. The seventh does not need to know it is seventh — it needs to know there is no room. Make the pressure readable and the number stops being needed, and each device holds its OWN line, which is right: a research task and a compile are not the same weight. The number's remaining job is DISPLAY (a reporter may show '6 live, historically the crawl line') and CALIBRATION of each device's own margin — never a gate. CORRECTION, 2026-08-04, same session, falsified by the relocation above: the test stated here — 'it becomes a manager the moment any device's decision routes through it' — IS TOO BROAD AND IS WRONG AS A GENERAL RULE. Every builder's decision routes through harbor_master's clearance, and that is the design, not a defect. The real line is INITIATIVE: a manager ASSIGNS, SCHEDULES, DISPATCHES; a gate answers when asked; a reporter shows. The boat decides to sail, the harbor says whether it is cleared, and the harbor never sails — harbor_master's own charter already says this ('the harbor clears the move, the crew sails it... a harbor that executed would be the ground_loop-executor goof'). What SURVIVES from the rule above, narrowly: nothing counts live builders, because nothing needs to — the resource question is answered from PRESSURE, not POPULATION, so no census is consulted by any gate and the list stays display-only.
known_consumers.why_memory_and_not_cpu: The first argument for mounting memory that is not 'we ought to have it'. The CPU reading here is `os.getloadavg()[0]` — a ONE-MINUTE DECAYING AVERAGE. A builder launched ten seconds ago is barely in it, so two devices asking in the same window can both be told yes. Memory has no such lag. FILED EDGE, not solved: the ask surface is racy by construction against a lagging metric, and the honest response is NOT a registry (see `no_manager_no_count` — refused) but the faster reading plus each asker holding its own margin. Recorded as a known property of the design, not a defect discovered later. Also unfixed by either: load average on Linux counts D-state (uninterruptible I/O wait), so this device's one metric moves for reasons it does not serve. RESOLVED 2026-08-04, and the resolution was the metric, not a margin. The lag was never intrinsic — it was an artifact of WHICH FIELD this device read. /proc/loadavg's fourth field (runnable/total) is instantaneous and sits in the same file as the average that lagged. MEASURED, 4 burners on this 8-core box: the runnable count went 2 -> 6 within one second while the 1-minute average went 5.5% -> 9.1% and was still reading 15.4% twelve seconds in. The sampler now serves runnable-over-cores and MemAvailable, both instantaneous. The race the 60s window was invented to survive mostly stops existing, and the 10s grant TTL now comfortably clears the floor it has to clear (a launch must become visible before the grant lapses, or the next asker is blind for the gap) — against the old metric, 10s would NOT have cleared it. The D-state contamination note stands and is now smaller: runnable counts R-state, so uninterruptible I/O wait no longer inflates the reading this device serves.
known_consumers.the_asker_is_harbor_master_not_the_build: RELOCATED by Akien, 2026-08-04, and it moves the whole surface: 'that means it's not asking the system anymore. it's asking the harbormaster, because that's the entity that would hold up the license to advance. and that's fine. we're still in the harbor!' A yes-with-a-deadline is a LICENSE, and licensing an advance is harbor_master's job already — its clearance gate (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py) binds three refusals before a cursor moves: UNAUTHORIZED (Law 6), UNPROVEN (Law 8), ILLEGAL (Law 4). Resource admission is a FOURTH — UNRESOURCED — on a gate that already exists, rather than a new gate with new authority. SO THIS DEVICE'S CONSUMER IS harbor_master, not the librarian and not a builder. The chain is builder -> harbor_master (license to advance) -> system_rackmount (is there room, by the harbor's line?). Two owner-gated doors in series, no third party, and NOTHING ANYWHERE COUNTS BUILDERS. The ask surface derived above is still the right shape and was on the wrong wall: the caller reaching it is the harbor, which wants a gate decision — which strengthens the verdict-not-number argument rather than weakening it. THE TTL IS RULED: 10 seconds ('the thing asks for it, and has 10 seconds to take it to the build gate'), which lands as an expiry on harbor_master's existing frozen per-operation Grant. BUILT 2026-08-04, both halves, in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py: `Unresourced` is the fourth refusal, and `Grant` now carries `issued_at` + `ttl_seconds` (GRANT_TTL_SECONDS = 10.0) with `GrantExpired` — a subclass of Unauthorized on purpose, so every guarantee that holds for 'no grant' holds identically for 'lapsed grant', including that the refused move leaves NO record. There is no way to mint an unexpiring grant: the window is a property of the capability, not an option a caller can decline. The harbor holds the LINES (HARBOR_LINES) and the system device holds the METRICS — the proof's fake resource owner RAISES on every door but `ask`, including every census shape, so a build that pulled a reading or counted builders dies on a path whose happy case is identical.
known_consumers.the_customer_for_the_raw_number_is_curio: The exported reading (x%) gets a named future consumer and an explicit not-yet: Akien, 2026-08-04 — 'we don't have a customer for cpu % now, so i'd be ok not to actually build it for now. but we'll want it at some point. i'm aiming to eventually put curiosity into this thing. and that will lead to self exploration.' A system exploring ITSELF is the first consumer that wants the number rather than a verdict, and it is not a control path — it is introspection. That is a DIFFERENT MENU SHAPE from the three already named: 'tell me about yourself', not 'may I' and not 'poke me when'. Exporting a reading down an introspection door costs nothing that Law 6 protects, because no one's gate depends on it. Down a CONTROL path it still costs the thing named in `the_access_mode_the_consumers_need`: the metric's semantics leak into every caller. Coarseness is a system setting and changeable (Akien, same message), so the number this door would export is not fixed either.

gates: proof gate — proofs/test_system_rackmount.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) the device serves a probe it did not advertise, or accepts a subscription to an unadvertised name instead of refusing loudly (CP1); (2) a poke fires when the host is UNDER the caller's line, or fails to fire when it is over (the predicate physics must be exact); (3) THE RAW READING CROSSES THE BUS — a poke body (or any envelope) carries the host metric rather than only that the line was crossed (Law 6 broken — the whole point); (4) the device pokes subscribers ITSELF rather than through its shim on the heartbeat pulse (re-absorbing the firing the shim owns), or re-grows a central scheduler / a trigger-kind enum; (5) `SystemRackmountDevice`/`SystemRackmountShim` stop subclassing `BaseDevice`/`BaseShim` / drop CP1-CP6, or `introspect()` stops reporting intention → state → settings in order.
how_it_learns: Yes. (1) The subscriptions + the pokes ARE the learning substrate: the device's state() surfaces who is waiting on which line (never the reading), and every poke is a why-bearing record on the bus — a threshold that never fires and one that fires constantly are both signals in the record, not in silence. (2) Law-6-local-evaluation is itself a learning stance: by keeping the host's data home and exporting only the wake-up, the system learns which host predicates it actually needs to advertise (cpu first, memory/disk as consumers ask) without ever coupling a consumer to the metric — the same start-narrow-and-let-evidence-widen discipline as sudo_relay's box. Its own horizon: the advertised menu (cpu today) and the level-triggered semantics are best-guesses-with-an-expiry — they firm up as real consumers (an ops device, the harvester, a memory-pressure watcher) subscribe. (3) RULED BY AKIEN 2026-08-05, and it is the biggest of the three — THE LINES THEMSELVES MUST BE LEARNED: 'system metrics should also be learning. we wanna watch what it costs to spin up another x, and in future be able to yeah/nay based on data, not a number out of akien's head. but even so, inference can be made: if no x running and 20% cpu, and 1 x = 30%, then we can say, from data, that we prolly don’t wanna go over 6 x. keeping an eye on it as we go of course.' THE METHOD, abstracted from his example: measure the BASELINE (the box with none of this thing running), measure the MARGINAL COST of one more, and divide the headroom by the margin to get the ceiling. Every term is observable; none of them is a number anyone has to hold in their head. THE WORKED EXAMPLE, corrected by Akien the same day he gave it: baseline 20%, and each additional x adds 10 POINTS — 1x=30%, 2x=40%, 3x=50%, 6x=80%, 'and leave some headroom for the system.' The 30% was a RUNNING TOTAL, not the marginal cost. That exposes a THIRD TERM the method needs and my first reading dropped: a RESERVE. ceiling = (usable_ceiling − baseline) / marginal, where usable_ceiling is 100 minus the headroom the host keeps for itself — (80 − 20) / 10 = 6. The reserve is not a rounding courtesy: it is the room the box needs to still be a box under the last admitted builder, and it is itself a learnable number. WHAT THIS RETIRES: harbor_master's HARBOR_LINES, both values, which are hand-set today (cpu 75.0 derived from Akien's measured 6-of-8 crawl point; memory 1024 a labelled hypothesis). It also puts a number on an ASSUMPTION hiding inside the 75: that one builder costs one runnable. On 8 cores, 10 points of runnable-over-cores is ~0.8 runnable per builder — so his example is CONSISTENT with that assumption rather than against it. Consistent is not measured; the measurement still decides, and until it runs the line is a guess with a good pedigree. CORRECTION OF RECORD 2026-08-05: I first read the 30% as the margin, which made the total 200% and led me to write here, and into the note and the slate, that the arithmetic was sayable only because runnable-over-cores has no 100% ceiling, and that his example implied ~2.4 runnable per builder. Both were mine, both wrong; 80% sits under a 100% ceiling fine. Kept visible rather than scrubbed because the mis-read IS the subject — Akien: 'this failure of communication is exactly why it's a progressively closer process.' The loss was at head→english, my capture was faithful to the wrong english, and what caught it was restating the arithmetic back to him in my own words. WHERE THE LEARNING COMES FROM — and this is the shape of the whole thing: the 6/8 number WAS a learned value all along. It was learned from experience, held in Akien's head, and had never been written down anywhere in either repo before 2026-08-04. So this is not new learning being invented; it is an existing learned value being moved out of a human's head and into data the system holds and keeps checking. 'keeping an eye on it as we go' is the standing part — a box's marginal cost is not a constant either (it moves with what else lives on the host), so the ceiling is a live derivation, not a one-time calibration. NOT BUILT, NOT TICKETED: captured 2026-08-05 as a note (CairnCommons/notes/) because Akien framed it as one, and the /intent door is his to fire.
traces_to: founding intention (get Akien out of running the system — a device gets a host trigger without a human wiring it)
Law 6 (the trigger is evaluated where its data is owned — the host reading never leaves the device; only the poke crosses the bus)
Law 4 (the poke fires by measured condition, not caller goodwill)
Law 5 (intent + code + proofs share this address)
the converged architecture (CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-heartbeat-probes-and-bus.md — the system device settles the A/B question → A: owner of host-resource predicates, not a scheduler)
cairn/tools/base/probe.py + cairn/tools/base/shim.py + cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/loop.py (the universal mechanism this device serves through)
cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py (the poke is a bus message)

cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py + cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector (this device is the emit surface's first real producer — the subscribe-gate breadcrumb it emits is what the inspector crawls; the complete-first-pass method measured in situ, Law 3)
Akien's correction 2026-07-18 (the rack is the chassis; the system rackmount is the system device, not a scheduler)
owner: CC owns the system_rackmount code + its proofs and gates writes to them. The system device OWNS the host-resource data it serves predicates on; that data is never exported, only pokes are — the owner-gate for host metrics, made physics.
proof: proofs/test_system_rackmount.py — it advertises the cpu_threshold menu and refuses an unadvertised name; end to end through the heartbeat, 'alert me at 80% CPU' pokes the subscriber's feed when over the line and no one when under, with the raw reading (95) crossing the bus nowhere (Law 6); the scheduler goof is gone (no service/scheduler API, no enum); device-hood + shim-hood + Form v0 #2 order. Composes the heartbeat + the real bus (db_domain) + the shim + the Probe. Green bare (python3) and under the tester. FLAKE FOUND + FIXED 2026-07-22 (a learning specimen, Law 8): the Law-6 leak-check scanned the WHOLE envelope for the reading '95', including the bus-assigned random uuid `id` — which contains the hex substring '95' ~12% of the time, so the proof went red ~2/8 by pure chance (a verdict decided by a coin toss, exactly what Law 8 forbids). Measured, not guessed: reproduced 2/8 under concurrency, the failing envelope's body was clean and the '95' sat in the uuid; the check now scopes to device-authored fields (excludes the transport-assigned id/date). Re-proven 0 red over 96 concurrent runs. The 'silent red' was a harness artifact (the earlier loop did not surface the subprocess stderr); under the tester the AssertionError was always captured.
provenance: Born 2026-07-18. First built (mislabeled) under the name `rack` — a 'rack' that was actually a trigger-firing scheduler; then re-homed as a SchedulerService under a service-abstraction framing (cairn 5cb593a). The design conversation with Akien (evening) corrected the model twice over: the rack is the chassis (bus + shims), and the system rackmount is not a scheduler at all but the SYSTEM DEVICE — the owner of host-resource predicates, serving threshold probes through the universal heartbeat + shim + bus. Reworked to that shape (built last in the heartbeat+probe+bus rework, composing every piece before it); the SchedulerService + trigger-kind enum deleted. A specimen of learning-its-gates: the identity was corrected by the owner before it hardened, and the code caught up to the corrected intention. Next: the spine resumes (MAP.md:892) — inference domain → web server.
learns: It does not; it is the system service manager — it starts and stops services without learning.
